_about: Sourced facts about music apps, for the 'visualizer for {app}' question pages (docs/seo.md, Phase 2d). Every fact has a sourceUrl and verifiedISO. Researched by sub-agents on 2026-11-02 and merged here by the lead agent.

apps.name: Spotify

visualizerFacts.text: Canvas is a short looping visual that artists can add to each of their tracks, not a visualiser.
In March 2014 Spotify stopped accepting new third-party apps for its desktop App Finder.
In February 2015 a desktop update phased out App Finder and third-party apps from the client.

apps.noVisualizerNote: We couldn't find a visualiser mentioned in Spotify's own help or download pages.

macApp.text: Spotify has a desktop app for the Mac.

webPlayer.text: Spotify plays in a browser at open.spotify.com.

other.text: In November 2024 Spotify cut off new apps from its Web API's audio-features and audio-analysis endpoints.

apps.name: YouTube Music

visualizerFacts.text: On a computer, YouTube Music runs as a web app, installable from Chrome; Google's help page for it doesn't mention a visualiser.
Visualisers for YouTube Music come from third-party browser extensions.

apps.noVisualizerNote: Google's help pages for YouTube Music on a computer don't mention a visualiser.

macApp.text: There's no official native Mac app; Google's route on a computer is the installable web app in Chrome.

webPlayer.text: It plays in a browser at music.youtube.com.

apps.name: TIDAL
apps.noVisualizerNote: We couldn't find a visualiser in TIDAL's support pages.

macApp.text: TIDAL has a desktop app for the Mac.
macApp.needsHandCheck: Read from a search snippet: the support site blocks automated reading. The page says macOS 14 or later; Homebrew's cask says 12 or later.

webPlayer.text: TIDAL plays in a browser, in Chrome, Safari, Firefox, Edge and others.

apps.name: SoundCloud

visualizerFacts.text: SoundCloud's player shows a waveform of the track, used for seeking and timed comments; it doesn't move with the music.
visualizerFacts.needsHandCheck: Read from a search snippet: the help centre blocks automated reading.

visualizerFacts.text: Visualisers for SoundCloud's web player come from third-party browser extensions.

apps.noVisualizerNote: SoundCloud's help pages don't mention a visualiser.

macApp.text: There's no native Mac app; SoundCloud's Desktop Player is the website installed as an app from Chrome, Brave or Edge.

webPlayer.text: It plays in a browser at soundcloud.com.

apps.name: Mixcloud

visualizerFacts.text: The visual Mixcloud documents is Mixcloud Live, where creators stream their own video, not a visualiser in the player.
For Mixcloud Live, a webcam is optional: visuals come from the creator.

apps.noVisualizerNote: We couldn't find a visualiser in Mixcloud's player in any of its pages we could read.

macApp.text: Mixcloud's App Store listing covers iPhone, iPad, Apple TV and Vision Pro, not the Mac; on a Mac it's the website.

webPlayer.text: Mixcloud plays in a browser at mixcloud.com, live streams included.

visualizerFacts.text: The Music app on the Mac has a visualiser: Window > Visualizer, with effects that change with the music.
It only visualises songs playing in the Music app, not Spotify, a browser or other apps.

macApp.text: The Music app is built into every Mac.

webPlayer.text: Apple Music also plays in a browser at music.apple.com.
webPlayer.needsHandCheck: Not from the researched sources; confirm the web player page.

apps.name: Deezer

visualizerFacts.text: What Deezer shows on a Mac is lyrics, in the desktop app and on deezer.com.
Deezer opened desktop lyrics to Free users in 2020.

apps.noVisualizerNote: Deezer's support pages don't mention a visualiser.

macApp.text: Deezer has a desktop app for the Mac, for macOS 12 or later.

webPlayer.text: Deezer plays in a browser at deezer.com.

visualizerFacts.text: VLC for Mac has built-in visualisations, turned on from Audio, then Visualizations.
VLC's visualizer effects are scope, spectrum, spectrometer and VU meter, with spectrum the default, drawn in a separate video window.
VLC's visualisations are filters on VLC's own audio output, so they show what VLC itself is playing.

macApp.text: VLC for Mac is a free download from VideoLAN, for Intel and Apple silicon Macs.

apps.name: Amazon Music

visualizerFacts.text: The visual Amazon documents for its web app is lyrics in the full-screen player, scrolling in time with the music.
visualizerFacts.needsHandCheck: An Amazon-owned help domain, not the usual amazon.com help URL: find the canonical page.

apps.noVisualizerNote: Amazon's help pages that we could read don't mention a visualiser.

macApp.text: Whether Amazon still offers a Mac desktop app is unclear: a February 2025 Amazon forum post, relayed on Apple's forums, says it was discontinued.
macApp.needsHandCheck: Amazon's own download page couldn't be read; check whether the Mac app is still offered.

webPlayer.text: Amazon Music plays in a browser at music.amazon.com, in Safari, Chrome, Firefox and Edge.
webPlayer.needsHandCheck: An Amazon-owned help domain, not the usual amazon.com help URL.

visualizerFacts.text: Plex lists visualisers as a Plex Pass premium music feature, in the apps that support them.
visualizerFacts.quote: Visualizers: Turn on one of multiple visualizers available in supported apps to re-live your old WinAmp days.

visualizerFacts.text: Plex's own music player Plexamp advertises over a dozen visualisers alongside four visual themes.
visualizerFacts.quote: MUSIC TO YOUR EYES Experience your music collection like you've never seen it before, with our UltraBlur backgrounds, over a dozen hypnotic visualizers, and four visual themes to satisfy every taste.

visualizerFacts.text: Plex says its visualisers are driven straight from the audio engine, so they react to the music with low latency.
visualizerFacts.quote: Visualizers are driven straight from the audio engine, at lower latency.

macApp.text: Plex has a native Mac desktop app, with more robust playback than its web app.
macApp.quote: Our Plex app for Windows and Mac computers is a standalone application that has the layout of our regular web app, but pairs it with much more robust playback capabilities as well as the ability to download items for offline use.

webPlayer.text: Plex plays in a browser through the Plex Web App player, which comes with Plex Media Server and needs no extra software.
webPlayer.quote: Plex Web App includes a player App, which allows you to access and play content directly inside a browser window. Because it's included with the Plex Media Server there's no additional software to download or install, making it a convenient way to watch your media.

other.text: Plex's own list of the Plex Web App Player controls covers playback, quality, audio, subtitles, chapters and the play queue, and no visualiser option appears among them.
other.quote: Choose the streaming quality to use

other.text: Searching Plex's own support library for visualizer returns only the iOS playback, Plex music, licence information and Plex Pass feature overview articles, so no document describes a visualiser for the web or Mac players.
Plex's iOS player documentation describes the visualiser as dynamic and based on the music being played back, with some visualisers such as Soundprint needing loudness data for the track.
other.quote: Visualizer - Enable a visualizer for your music. Most are dynamic and based on the music being played back. Some, like the Soundprint, require the track to have loudness data. (Plex Pass feature)

apps.name: Twitch

visualizerFacts.text: Twitch's player shows the broadcaster's own broadcast rather than a visual Twitch draws itself, since the channel page guide describes the video screen as where the broadcast is displayed.
The animated overlays Twitch ships are alerts for stream events such as followers, subscriptions, Bits, raids and Hype Trains, with no alert type tied to the audio of the stream.
Extra visuals in a Twitch stream come from third-party Extensions, because Twitch states that most Extensions are built by third-party developers even though the underlying technology is Twitch's.

apps.noVisualizerNote: Twitch's help centre has no visualiser feature of its own, with searches for visualiser returning no articles, so any visuals on a music stream come from the broadcaster or from third-party tools.

macApp.text: There is no native Twitch app for macOS: its App Store listing covers iPhone, iPad and Apple TV.
macApp.quote: There is no native Twitch app for macOS, as Apple's App Store listing for Twitch: Live Streaming gives the platforms as iPhone, iPad, Apple TV and iMessage, and the app has no Mac App Store page.

webPlayer.text: Twitch is watched in a desktop web browser at twitch.tv, which supports the latest Chrome, Firefox, Edge, Safari and Opera.
webPlayer.quote: Twitch is watched in a desktop web browser at twitch.tv, and Twitch's help centre says the desktop web browser experience of twitch.tv officially supports the two latest versions of Google Chrome and Mozilla Firefox, the most recent version of Microsoft Edge, the most recent version of Apple Safari and the most recent version of Opera and Opera GX.

other.text: Twitch's developer documentation describes an Extension as a webpage that sits inside Twitch and communicates with Twitch to provide extra functionality, with an overlay type that displays on top of the whole video as a transparent overlay.
Searching the Twitch help centre for visualiser returns no articles, so the service documents no visualiser of its own.
Music on Twitch is made up of broadcaster channels, with the music directory at twitch.tv/music listing live channels such as lofi and DJ streams.
